description: Reconciliation of the apparent contradiction between one-step TEST-B R²=-2.609 and rollout R²=0.978.

contradiction.apparent_contradiction: How can one-step prediction be worse than mean predictor while multi-step rollout is near-perfect?

root_cause.one_step_evaluation: Used ALL 420 TEST-B records (60 realized + 360 counterfactual)
root_cause.rollout_evaluation: Used ONLY realized records (48 at h=1) with trajectory filtering
root_cause.counterfactual_contamination: 360 counterfactual records have delta magnitude 3.517 (35x larger than realized at 0.110)

reconciliation.explanation: The one-step R² was contaminated by counterfactual records. On realized records only, one-step R²=0.982 matches rollout R²=0.978.

deeper_finding.implication: The high absolute R² is inflated by low variance of state changes. The zero-delta predictor (predict no change) already gets R²=0.927. The model's delta predictions are worse than mean-delta (delta R²=-0.24). The absolute R² is NOT a meaningful metric for this task.
deeper_finding.correct_metric: Delta R² on invariant dimensions only, compared against zero-delta baseline

methodology_corrections.training: Train on REALIZED records only (not counterfactual)
methodology_corrections.primary_metric: Delta R² on invariant dimensions, not absolute R²
methodology_corrections.state_decomposition: Split state into invariant/context/derived and evaluate Δz_invariant separately
